races.name: Queen Anne Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Cicero's Gift
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who is mapped to midfield solely because there are too many front-runners to accommodate — he will attempt to press forward early but likely ends up racing in a more restrained position than ideal; three wins from nine on good ground and a solid recent form string of 211 make him a threat if he does find position.
runners_data.comment: Cicero's Gift has won twice in its last five starts and acts on soft, good and AW, but the ground here may be on the quick side for this one, and last time out's seventh in the Lockinge — beaten over seven lengths — tempers enthusiasm despite that Group 1 backdrop.

runners_data.name: Damysus
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer mapped to midfield due to the crowded front-end landscape; his 7/24 trainer strike rate for Gosden and two wins from eight on similar going give him strong claims if James Doyle manoeuvres him into a forward pitch early, and his recent drop back to a mile from further trips looks well-timed.
runners_data.comment: Damysus arrives on the back of a 6¼-length thumping in a Group 1 at Newbury last time, with lack of pace exposed over a mile, and today's test looks similarly sharp for a horse who really comes into his own at nine or ten furlongs.

runners_data.name: Docklands
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who is shown in midfield only because the race shape cannot accommodate every front-runner; Harry Eustace's sharp 1/10 trainer form and Mark Zahra's aggressive riding style mean Docklands is worth watching for an early forward move — the gelding's sole win from 13 on good-to-soft going and a recent return to form (1-3) suggests he is peaking.
runners_data.comment: Docklands won this race last year and shaped with promise on return when a close third in a Group 1 at Sha Tin 51 days ago, so course-and-distance form reads well; first-time headgear and a trainer in form add appeal, though a rating of 118 versus our figure of 114 suggests the handicapper holds a slight edge.

runners_data.name: First Conquest
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer mapped to midfield by race shape; Ryan Moore's presence is a significant positive as he excels at finding position in competitive fields, but a 179-day absence since last run is a material concern and his consistent placed form (33433) suggests he finishes rather than wins these races.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and absent for 179 days, First Conquest shaped respectably with a close third in a Meydan Group 2 last time but looks likely to fill a pacemaking role for better-fancied stablemates here, making it very hard to fancy at big odds.

runners_data.name: More Thunder
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent type likely to secure a forward berth behind Opera Ballo; Tom Marquand's 11/30 trainer strike for Haggas is strong, and More Thunder's versatility across 6-8f on good ground with four wins from eight similar-ground runs makes him a leading player if the pace quickens.
runners_data.comment: Ran a career-best when runner-up in the Lockinge Group 1 last time, showing real progression at a mile on a sound surface, and this stiff track could bring him even closer to the principals — though there's a nagging question over whether that ceiling has now been reached.

runners_data.name: Notable Speech
runners_data.note: Races prominently and is likely to travel in the first two or three under Buick; Charlie Appleby's 1/10 trainer form is low but Notable Speech's three wins from seven on firm/good-to-firm and a top-of-the-ground preference (going tag OK, TS data supports fast surfaces) make him extremely well-suited to today's conditions.
runners_data.comment: Notable Speech has won five G1s and was imperious when scooting clear in the Lockinge last time, marking it out as probably the world's number-one miler; carrying 128 lb from stall 1, the course record is a minor query but fast ground suits and this is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Opera Ballo
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and likely to lead unchallenged from the start; five wins from nine on good going, an unblemished recent form string of 121-11, and no headgear concerns make him the pivotal horse in any pace analysis — the race shape fits him perfectly but his odds are likely to reflect it.
runners_data.comment: Four wins in its last five starts, Opera Ballo has progressed into one of Europe's leading milers — most recently dictating and winning the bet365 Mile (Group 2) at Sandown by 3l from a multiple G1 winner — and acts on today's conditions. First-time headgear is the one unknown.

runners_data.name: Ten Bob Tony
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who is mapped to midfield because of the crowded front-end; only 10 days since his last run which could indicate a quick-fire campaign or fitness concerns, and his form over shorter trips (6-7f) on soft/good-to-soft is patchy — today's flat mile on good to firm looks a stiff ask.
runners_data.comment: Ten Bob Tony won a Group 3 at Epsom ten days ago, but that victory came on ground with cut and this looks a stiffer test — rated 108 on our figures and ranked last of nine, there are serious doubts about whether it can match those elite rivals here.

runners_data.name: Zeus Olympios
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with three wins from six on good going and a clear preference for this exact trip and surface; form figures of 111-33 suggest a horse who wins when conditions suit but has hit a form ceiling at the top level — Clifford Lee takes over and the 7/46 trainer strike for Burke over 14 days is modest.
runners_data.comment: Zeus Olympios arrives on the back of a career-best effort when finishing third in the Lockinge Stakes, and his three wins in his last five starts underline a horse in fine fettle — the main reservation is whether he can quite bridge the gap to outright Group 1 winning class today.

races.paceDynamic: Opera Ballo is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a nine-runner field, he is likely to stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead from the break under Billy Loughnane, controlling tempo from the front at a rhythm that suits his hold-up-converted style — his five wins from nine on similar ground underline how well this setup fits him. More Thunder and Notable Speech are the natural challengers from a prominent pitch, likely to sit close behind Opera Ballo and apply pressure from the three-furlong pole, turning this into a true test of finishing quality rather than raw stamina. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can all secure their natural position — Damysus, Docklands, Cicero's Gift, First Conquest and Ten Bob Tony are all mapped to midfield not by preference but by sheer traffic, and those who successfully establish closer ground early (most likely Damysus and Docklands given their handlers) will hold a material advantage. A controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground over a flat mile at Ascot overwhelmingly favours runners who can race prominently or sit just off the pace with a high cruising speed, with genuine hold-up horses facing the hardest task of all.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Opera Ballo Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Opera Ballo leads unbothered and sets a steady-to-honest fractions throughout, dictating from the front.
scenarios.body: Opera Ballo's five wins from nine on similar going, combined with uncontested front-running at Ascot's flat mile, means he can set his own terms and sprint clear from two furlongs out before rivals can close; his Charlie Appleby/Billy Loughnane combination thrives in these controlled-tempo Group 1s.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pressure Lifts Prominent Challengers
scenarios.trigger: If More Thunder or Damysus pushes the pace from the second furlong, injecting genuine tempo and forcing Opera Ballo to quicken earlier than ideal.
scenarios.body: A faster pace plays into the hands of horses with a high cruising speed and tactical reserve, notably Notable Speech and Zeus Olympios, who can travel with minimal fuss and unleash a strong final furlong; Damysus's recent course form over this trip on similar ground also positions him well if he secures a forward berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Runner Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the nominally midfield-mapped prominent types — Docklands or Cicero's Gift — successfully secures a front-rank position and benefits from the controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: Docklands has a win from 13 runs on comparable going and Harry Eustace's recent 1/10 trainer strike rate signals a live runner; Cicero's Gift won three of his last five on good ground and jumping to the front of this smaller-field scenario could transform him from traffic victim to pace beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong from the front and the field strings out, creating a clean gap for a late charger.
scenarios.body: Zeus Olympios, dropping back from winning trips of 8f at Group level on good ground and carrying strong form figures of 111 over this distance, has the profile to produce a powerful late run if the tempo burns rivals out; however, Ascot's flat mile rarely rewards deep closers and this remains a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Opera Ballo secures an uncontested lead — if he is not pressed before halfway, his front-running record on good ground at this distance makes him very difficult to peg back.

Monitor how many of the redistributed prominent types (Damysus, Docklands, Cicero's Gift) attempt to push forward at the start — a scrappy, compressed early phase could unsettle their rhythm and compromise their finishing position.
First Conquest's 179-day lay-off is a significant fitness flag; Ryan Moore may be conservative early which could leave the horse with too much to do in a race unlikely to produce a strong late pace.

Ten Bob Tony's quick 10-day turnaround after a flat run deserves monitoring in the paddock — any sign of a below-par coat or restricted movement should downgrade his chances in a field of this quality.

Notable Speech's trainer strike rate of 1/10 over 14 days for Appleby is unusually low — cross-reference with Notable Speech's going preferences as any overnight rain softening the ground could flip his form profile negatively given his best performances have come on firm or fast surfaces.

races.name: Coventry Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Adaay Of Scarlett
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-runner who has won twice from three starts over 5f on Good, but with this volume of handy types is likely to be pushed back into midfield; Billy Loughnane rides and the step up to 6f on Ascot's stiff track is an unknown.
runners_data.comment: Rattled off back-to-back wins before a game half-length second in Listed company latest, and acts on today's going and distance, making this high-class colt a genuine threat — the main concern is whether he's now near his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Arizona Raider
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-runner who will struggle to hold position in this traffic and faces being shuffled to midfield; won over 8f on Good last time which raises a stamina angle but also a serious pace-style question over 6f in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Roscommon auction race last time on the step up in trip and drop in class, but ranks near the foot of the weights here and looks vulnerable at this level, with sounder ground at least suiting his action.

runners_data.name: Bull Shark
runners_data.note: Genuine unknowns in running style — four runs have produced four placed efforts including a second over 7f on Good, which hints at stamina rather than pure speed; David Egan rides and this horse may prove best suited by a truly-run race where relentlessness matters.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but not without appeal — Bull Shark quickened clear latest at The Curragh only to be caught late, suggesting timing rather than ability was the issue. A very useful sprint prospect who acts on varying ground, though ranked 18th on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-runner who is effectively a debutant in pattern class with only a second over 6f on Good to his name; Joe Leavy takes the ride and redistribution into midfield is likely, leaving his chance heavily dependent on a strong pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Cilician shaped with distinct promise on debut, going down by just half a length at Nottingham over today's trip, and speed in the pedigree suggests the six furlongs suits; however, winless in recent starts and carrying 129lb from stall 9, there's still plenty to find at this level.

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-runner for Aidan O'Brien and Ryan Moore who won over 6f on Good at the highest juvenile level, but in a field of this size is likely to be taken back into midfield unless Moore elects to be aggressive; the top-level form is the key credential here.
runners_data.comment: Confucius took a Naas maiden by four lengths last time, that form already looking solid, and he gets the nod from the top course jockey in a yard that won this 12 months ago; open to further progress and the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Cut A Dash
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-runner for Richard Hannon and Sean Levey who is unbeaten in one start over 5f on Good, but that lightly raced profile and redistribution into midfield creates significant doubt about how he handles Ascot's demands under competition.
runners_data.comment: Won on debut at York with plenty in hand, quickening clear cosily by three lengths on good ground over today's trip, and that novice form looks strong enough to merit this step up in class — the sole risk is how she handles 34 days off and the rise in grade.

runners_data.name: Easy Answer
runners_data.note: Unknown running style with only a third over 6f on Good to his name; Cristian Demuro rides for Michael Bell and the lightly raced profile means this horse is almost entirely an unknown quantity in terms of how he will handle a big competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with plenty of promise on debut at Yarmouth, finishing third — best of those held up — beaten just 1¼ lengths, and should improve stepping forward from that initial experience if ridden more positively over today's trip, though winless in recent starts remains the caveat.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: Unknown running style with only a second over 6f on Good from one run, and the headgear flag (h) needs monitoring; Faleh Bughenaim rides for Hamad Al Jehani and this is a speculative entry stepping into Group 2 company with minimal evidence.
runners_data.comment: Promising debut second at Lingfield, beaten 3l while finishing well after being outpaced, suggests ability — first-time headgear adds interest — but stepping up in class leaves Final Objective looking vulnerable despite that speed pedigree over today's trip.

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-runner who won over 6f on Good on debut, but William Buick and the redistribution into midfield here may actually suit him if he can produce a sharp finishing effort; lightly raced but the James Ferguson operation has strong Ascot juvenile form.
runners_data.comment: Scored on debut at Newbury, quickening well to win by 1¼l, but that maiden form reads nothing special and our figures rank it well below most here — further progress needed to compete at this level.

runners_data.name: Great Barrier Reef
runners_data.note: Prominent-runner with back-to-back wins over 6f on Good and Soft for Aidan O'Brien, Wayne Lordan takes the ride and this horse has the profile to secure an early prominent position before many rivals; arguably the horse best placed to track The Scallionator directly.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins culminate in a Curragh Group 3 success last time, where he had a bit in hand and looked like 7f is well within compass — stiff track, sound surface and proven distance all in his favour, with the yard having won this last year. The main risk is handling a large field from stall 3.

runners_data.name: High King
runners_data.note: Prominent-runner who won over 6f on Good last time for Donnacha O'Brien, Gavin Ryan rides and a debut 12th suggests improvement since; short enough turnaround at 19 days is worth noting but the trainer is in form and this horse is capable of sitting just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Franked a taking Fairyhouse win with an excellent turn of foot, and that 3½-length success reads well stepping up in class; the unplaced run on the other side of that coin and a stiff 129lb are the checks on enthusiasm here.

runners_data.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners_data.note: Unknown running style with three placed efforts all over 5f on Good for Clive Cox; the step up to 6f may actually assist this horse's stamina profile, and Rossa Ryan is an astute jockey in competitive fields, but no win yet is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but winless in recent starts, Jaan Ki Tukri has placed in all three latest outings and acts on today's going and distance — though stepping up in class looks the key test from stall 22 off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Kamaal
runners_data.note: Unknown running style with only a fifth over 6f on Good from a single start, and is flagged as lightly raced with no placed efforts; Cieren Fallon rides for Jack Jones and this is realistically the most speculative runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and beaten three lengths on a modest Newbury maiden debut 32 days ago, Kamaal looks out of depth stepping up in class here, though today's trip and going hold no fears — a big ask at the foot of the weights.

runners_data.name: Mrair
runners_data.note: Prominent-runner who won over 6f on Good last time and ran second on debut at the same trip, giving Oisin Murphy one of the most straightforward recent form profiles in the race; the horse's ability to sit close and quicken is proven and this is a serious contender.
runners_data.comment: Won a Lingfield novice by 3l on latest but that came in weaker company, and greenness remains a concern under 129lb from stall 14; with a trainer in form and more improvement likely as experience grows, the upside is real if inexperience doesn't cost.

runners_data.name: Night In Vegas
runners_data.note: Prominent-runner who has won twice consecutively including over 6f on Good, Charles Bishop rides for Eve Johnson Houghton who is in good form at 5/26 over 14 days; 25 days since last run is within normal parameters and this horse has a clean tactical profile.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins, including a smooth Goodwood success last time, give Night In Vegas solid claims, and the step up in class looks the obvious next test; acts on good and effective at today's trip, though 129 lb from stall 21 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Royal Heritage
runners_data.note: Prominent-runner who won over 6f on Soft on debut for Hamad Al Jehani, James Doyle takes the ride and the very short six-day turnaround from last run is a significant flag to watch; only one run means the form line is thin but Doyle's booking is a positive signal.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye with a comfortable 3-length debut win at Hamilton six days ago and acts on good to soft over this trip, but the quick turnaround and a provisional rating of 102 ranked 15th of 22 suggest there are open questions — an improver worth noting, albeit untested beyond that promising maiden.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Pride
runners_data.note: Unknown running style who won over 5f on Good on debut for K R Burke, James McDonald rides and the lightly raced flag applies; the step up to 6f and the leap to Group 2 from a single 5f maiden win is a substantial ask however well the yard is operating.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up on debut at Ayr and that form has been franked, marking this one out as potentially very useful stepping up in class; acts on the going and trip, though the hefty 129lb and draw 17 are factors to weigh against a short sample of evidence.

runners_data.name: Siouxperb
runners_data.note: Prominent-runner who won over 6f on Good for Archie Watson, Hector Crouch rides and the 56-day break since last run is the longest fresher in the field — that absence is a key watch point for whether the horse returns in peak condition.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up by four lengths on debut at Yarmouth, quickening clear with plenty in hand, and stays today's trip on this ground — a smart prospect returning off a short break, though 129 lb and 56 days off give rivals something to aim at.

runners_data.name: The Ginger Kid
runners_data.note: Prominent-runner who won over 6f on Good last time and endured a distant 13th on debut at the same trip, suggesting a horse who has improved sharply; Kieran Shoemark rides for Ed Walker who is 6/32 over 14 days and this horse's quick turnaround at 13 days needs monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Followed up debut experience with a narrow novice win at Nottingham 13 days ago, but this represents a sharp step up in grade and, ranked 16th of 22 on our figures, considerably more improvement will be needed to make an impact here.

runners_data.name: The Harv
runners_data.note: Prominent-runner who won over 6f on Soft on debut for M D O'Callaghan, Colin Keane takes the ride and the nine-day turnaround is extremely tight and the single soft-ground run means Good to Firm conditions are an untested variable.
runners_data.comment: Scraped home by a nose on debut at Goodwood nine days ago, with the form nothing special and the win flattered by a pace collapse — hard to fancy at the foot of the weights on these figures, though the scope to progress with that run under its belt offers the only realistic hook.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner in this race, has won over 6f on Good and placed twice at the same trip; Wesley Joyce for Michael Mulvany and the horse's ability to control tempo from the front without being seriously pressured is the central pace dynamic — all tactical assessments flow from this horse's fractions.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Listowel maiden by three lengths 16 days ago and is clearly progressing, though carrying 129lb from stall 16 is a notable ask stepping into stronger company; breeding points to 6f/7f on good ground as the sweet spot, so conditions at least play to strengths.

runners_data.name: Treasurer
runners_data.note: Unknown running style with only a fourth over 6f on Good from a single run, and flagged as lightly raced with no placed or winning efforts; Rowan Scott rides for Charlie Fellowes and this is effectively an exploratory entry with very limited evidence to work from.
runners_data.comment: Promising 3l fourth on debut at Nottingham shows ability, and today's trip and conditions suit, but ranked 19th of 22 on our figures, Treasurer has plenty to find in this company despite likely improvement still to come.

races.paceDynamic: The Scallionator is the confirmed front-runner and will look to dictate from the gates on Good to Firm ground over Ascot's straight six, setting a sustainable but honest gallop that is unlikely to be seriously pressured for the lead. However, this 22-runner field is absolutely loaded with prominent-running types — Great Barrier Reef, High King, Mrair, Night In Vegas, Siouxperb, The Ginger Kid, The Harv, Adaay Of Scarlett, Arizona Raider, Cilician, Confucius, Cut A Dash and God Given Talent all want to race handily, meaning a significant number will be forced to settle deeper than their natural position. With one genuine pacesetter and a bunched, competitive prominent pack racing at a brisk but controlled tempo on quick ground, the race sets up for horses who can travel in the first half of the field, pick up momentum in the final two furlongs and sustain their effort to the line — prominent and midfield types with a strong finishing kick will be best served, while pure hold-up horses face a stern task getting to the front in time. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their favoured position; Great Barrier Reef (Ryan Moore stablemate Confucius aside, Aidan O'Brien's primary 6f weapon here), Mrair, and Night In Vegas are best positioned — by draw, jockey profile and recent tactical evidence — to secure the prominent slots closest to The Scallionator.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If The Scallionator sets a fair pace and the prominent pack settles just off the leader, producing a strongly-run but not suicidal tempo.
scenarios.body: The horses who travel in the first two to three lengths of the leader will get first run and the Good to Firm surface will favour those with tactical speed over pure closers; Mrair, Great Barrier Reef and Night In Vegas all fit this profile with their ability to sit close and quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, leaders outstay
scenarios.trigger: If The Scallionator controls the tempo conservatively and the prominent pack fails to exert real pressure, turning it into a tactical sprint.
scenarios.body: A slow early gallop compresses the field and the premium shifts to pure sprint speed and positional advantage; horses already on the heels of the leader will have first use of the rail or stands-side ground at the death.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers benefit from pace meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If the sheer number of prominent types creates a fierce early scrimmage, burning out those who push forward too hard in the first half of the race.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed to midfield who have a genuine turn of foot — God Given Talent, Adaay Of Scarlett and Cut A Dash — will be coiled and primed to mow down a tiring front rank over the final furlong on quick ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Draw or group bias decisive
scenarios.trigger: If a strong bias develops toward one side of the track in the straight, rendering positional and stylistic profiles secondary to draw and group alignment.
scenarios.body: With 22 runners inevitably splitting into groups, any horse caught on the unfavoured side will be compromised regardless of form; those drawn centrally or toward the favoured rail and travelling prominently will have an insurmountable structural advantage.

watchPoints.text: The Scallionator is the sole confirmed front-runner — if Wesley Joyce is able to dictate an uncontested lead at a controlled tempo, this horse becomes a serious player rather than just a pacemaker and all other pace assessments depend on the fractions he sets.

Royal Heritage has a six-day turnaround from last run, which is unusually tight for a juvenile stepping into Group 2 company; watch whether James Doyle settles the horse smoothly or whether the short recovery shows in the early exchanges.

Siouxperb has been off the track for 56 days — the longest absence in the field — and while Archie Watson is capable of producing a horse fresh, this represents a meaningful fitness and racecourse-sharpness unknown in a 22-runner sprint.

The sheer volume of prominent-runners redistributed to midfield — God Given Talent, Confucius, Cut A Dash, Adaay Of Scarlett and Arizona Raider among them — means the first two furlongs could involve significant jostling for position, and any horse caught wide or shuffled back abruptly in that phase is compromised for the rest of the race.

Draw and group formation will be critical in a 22-runner straight-six at Ascot; watch which group splits form at the start and whether a bias toward stands or far side emerges, as this has historically overridden form considerations at Royal Ascot in large-field sprint fields.

races.name: King Charles III Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Ain't Nobody
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Kevin Stott and Kevin Ryan; best on similar going (1W in last 3 comparable runs) and will relish the strong pace this field should generate, though needs things to go right in a 26-runner sprint.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and again disappointing at York last time, Ain't Nobody is very erratic and not always resolute, though first-time headgear may sharpen focus, and it does hold course-and-distance form on today's ground.

runners_data.name: American Affair
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner for Jim Goldie; three wins from five on similar going at this trip, but Paul Mulrennan must secure position early against fierce competition for the same ground — not straightforward from a wide gate.|
runners_data.comment: Won this race last year and arrives in decent nick after finishing second in a Group 2 on latest start, so course-and-distance form stacks up well; the 133 lb burden from stall 18 is the obvious query, though a progressive return to form suggests fitness is no concern.

runners_data.name: Big Mojo
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the race; Tom Marquand will look to control from the front, but he won't be alone and his recent form shows a decline (7th last time) after a peak win at 6f — dropping to 5f on quick ground is a question mark.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 2 last time out, that run probably needed after 34 days off, Big Mojo is well-suited by today's 6f on fast ground and holds strong claims off 117 — the risk is getting caught too far back again as last year here showed.

runners_data.name: Cover Up
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner who has won four times on similar going; 80 days off the track (hg: t — tongue-tie) is worth noting, and James McDonald's booking adds considerable confidence, but the layoff and the 6f-heavy history must be weighed.|
runners_data.comment: Held every chance on form credentials — acts on any going over 5f — but well held in a Group 1 last time and ranks 22nd of 26 on our figures; the first-time headgear and 80-day break add further uncertainty for a horse that simply may not be up to this level.

runners_data.name: Getreadytorumble
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more early-speed types than can all get their position — in reality Jack Channon's horse will face a tough battle to race where he wants to.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 2 last time — fair enough form — and Listed-placed with good prior profile, but ranked 21 of 26 on our figures and needs more improvement again to trouble these; the wide draw in a large field adds no help.

runners_data.name: Jakajaro
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner mapped to midfield due to race shape congestion; two wins on good ground over 5f recently for Robert Cowell gives him solid course profile claims, but Jamie Spencer will need to find a way through if shuffled back.|
runners_data.comment: Shaped well when fourth in a Group 2 last time, going down by just 1¼ lengths only near the finish, and two wins in its last five starts show the progressive profile — yet stepping into this grade still leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner pushed back to midfield on the map by the race's pace saturation; Quinn's six-year-old has form at the trip on good ground but recent form is patchy (0 from 4 in last four starts), so this is a tough spot.|
runners_data.comment: Shock Group 2 winner last year, but JM Jungle has failed to recapture that form this season, beaten seven lengths in a Group 2 last time — hard to fancy at these weights from stall 14, even if the trip and going hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Night Raider
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner on a hot streak (2 wins from last 2); K R Burke in excellent form (T14: 7/46) and James Doyle takes the ride — two wins on similar going, but faces the same early crowding issue as all prominent types here.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins culminate in a career-best Temple Stakes Group 2 success at Haydock last time out, and with conditions and trip squarely in favour, Night Raider arrives in fine trim just 24 days later — the main risk is whether the bold front-running style holds up at this level.

runners_data.name: Overpass
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner; second-highest rated at OR 116, Australian-trained by Bjorn Baker and lightly raced on British turf, with good 6f/7f form but this 5f trip on Good to Firm is a step into the unknown — the drop in distance is the key query.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent G1 performer whose T J Smith Stakes fourth (beaten 2l) sets the standard here, and dropping in trip to a stiff track plays to his strengths; yet to win in recent starts but rates clear top on our figures and will be tough to peg back.

runners_data.name: Rumstar
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner for Portman; two wins on similar going at this trip, recent second last time out (2/5f/GOO) suggests he is in form — Rob Hornby could get a clean run if he slots in just behind the speed.|
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a close second in a Group 3 on fast ground latest, and suits today's trip and conditions well; yet to score in recent starts and faces a stiff ask at this level after being outclassed here last year, but is clearly in better shape now.

runners_data.name: Shagraan
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner shown in midfield because the race shape cannot accommodate all the front-types; Clive Cox's five-year-old has three wins on similar ground including a recent one, and Hector Crouch could find a pocket if traffic allows.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite last time in the Temple Stakes but holds Listed-class form over this trip and going — a multiple winner at this level who retains claims stepping back from Group company, though that Haydock flop leaves a question mark hanging over current form.

runners_data.name: Starlust
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner for Ralph Beckett; no wins in last 15 on similar going (0W3P) and recent form string includes three singles in the 6s/7s — in-form trainer but this horse's record suggests a struggle to land the blow.|
runners_data.comment: Showed Group 1 class and ran encouragingly in this race last year, but winless in recent starts and must prove that sharpness is back after a stud sabbatical; the Carlisle Listed run 17 days ago should strip fitness forward.

runners_data.name: Asfoora
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner for Lemos De Souza; three career wins on similar going but last two outings were disappointing (12th and 10th on soft and good), and blinkers/tongue-tie headgear worn — needs to rediscover earlier form.|
runners_data.comment: Defends her 2024 crown here, but two unplaced efforts this term — including a poor showing on easy ground at Haydock last time — raise questions about current form; the tongue-tie is new, fast ground suits, and a bounce-back from this proven G1 winner can't be dismissed.

runners_data.name: Azure Angel
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner mapped to midfield due to race congestion; won at this trip on standard going and wore blinkers/tongue-tie (hg: tb) — Daniel Tudhope rides, but form figures show inconsistency (5,1,6,1,8) and last run was 5th.|
runners_data.comment: Azure Angel steps up sharply in class after a creditable Listed effort last time, but at 130 lb from stall 25 and ranked 24 of 26 on our figures, the step into this grade looks a tough ask — first-time blinkers are a plus, though.

runners_data.name: First Instinct
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner redistributed to midfield because the field is overloaded with pace; William Haggas yard in form (T14: 11/30) and Cieren Fallon rides, but 45-day absence and recent 9th/13th runs leave questions.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a G3 success in recent starts but has disappointed twice since, including a 6½-length beating last time out 45 days ago; acts on today's going and distance, yet improvement is needed if that winning form is to resurface.

runners_data.name: Frost At Dawn
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner shown in midfield on the map due to race shape; wears a visor (hg: v) and has only 1 win from 15 on similar ground — William Buick's booking is eye-catching but the record on Good to Firm is weak.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and below-par at Haydock last time on easy ground, Frost At Dawn has the course-and-distance form and wears first-time cheekpieces that may spark a revival, though a disappointing 2025 campaign so far leaves plenty to prove from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner redistributed to midfield; very limited record on similar going (2/15, 0W1P), most form coming on all-weather or soft — Good to Firm is a genuine concern and this looks a very tough ask at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten just 2¼ lengths when second at York latest, Heavenly Heather has been progressive, but ranked last of 26 on our figures and drawn in stall 22, this looks a big ask at the weights.

runners_data.name: Mgheera
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner shown in midfield because there is no room; Ed Walker's six-year-old has a modest record on similar going (5/15, 2W3P) and recent outings have been mid-division finishes — hard to see how Kieran Shoemark finds a way to the front.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and ranked well down our figures in a competitive field, Mgheera does at least have course-and-distance form on today's going and shaped with credit when beaten two lengths in a Group 2 last time, hinting at residual class.

runners_data.name: Miss Attitude
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Jack Channon; wears a tp (tongue-tie/pad) combination, won last time over this trip on good ground (1/5f/GOO), and the strong pace should play to her strengths — Ronan Whelan to thread through a big field.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 3 last time after missing the break, Miss Attitude's recent form reads consistently enough but she needs more to be competitive at this level, and ranked near the foot of our assessments, first-time cheekpieces must do the heavy lifting from stall 16.

runners_data.name: Monteille
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from Italy (Mario Baratti); concerning record on similar going (3/15, 0W0P — no wins at all on comparable ground), 80-day absence, and Cristian Demuro flies in — needs everything to go right and the going record is a serious red flag.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent Group winner in France who ran creditably when beaten two lengths in a Group 1 last time out, but fast ground remains a concern and the 80-day absence gives pause — capable of mixing it, though conditions may again blunt the edge.

runners_data.name: Rayevka
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner redistributed to midfield because the field shape forces it; Graffard's four-year-old filly won last time on soft and has limited good-ground form (0W1P) — Barzalona's experience might help her find a slot forward.|
runners_data.comment: Rayevka arrives in form after a convincing Group 3 win at Longchamp 37 days ago, benefitting from a drop in trip and grade, and ran well at this very meeting last year — stiff 5f on today's going looks ideal, though 130lb and a field of 26 pose stiff tasks.

runners_data.name: Rosy Affair
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner shown in midfield on the map due to pace saturation; George Boughey's five-year-old has three wins on similar going, mostly at 6f rather than 5f, and Billy Loughnane should be aggressive to secure position.|
runners_data.comment: Rosy Affair arrives on the back of a Listed win at Haydock 25 days ago and has won three of her last five starts, but stepping up in class looks the key question for this progressive mare, who handles today's trip and conditions well enough.

runners_data.name: Time For Sandals
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner for Harry Eustace; form figures showing consistent mid-field finishes (8,5,7,3,1), mostly at 6f on good ground — the drop to 5f is a slight concern and Richard Kingscote will need to improve on recent finishing positions.|
runners_data.comment: Landed the Commonwealth Cup at this very meeting 12 months ago, so course form reads perfectly, and a trainer firing on all cylinders adds to the appeal after a first-run reappearance at York that arguably underflattered — there should be more to come. The wide draw from stall 9 is the one factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Aspect Island
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner pushed to midfield by race shape; three-year-old for James Owen (T14: 11/47 — trainer flying) wearing a visor, with solid placed form (three 3rds) on similar going but no win at this level yet.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent sprinter who ran a game race when a close third in Listed company last time out, but has been placed at the highest level and this demands even more again; the first-time visor is an interesting move, though, and 117 on our ratings suggests there's ability to exploit.

runners_data.name: Behike
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner mapped to midfield by the race's pace congestion; lightly raced three-year-old (just three runs) with back-to-back wins, latest over 6f on good ground — David Egan rides and the unexposed profile is intriguing.|
runners_data.comment: Boasts back-to-back wins including a cosy novice success at Lingfield last time, but steps up sharply in grade now and, ranked 20th of 26 in the field, this looks a big ask so early in its career.

runners_data.name: Mission Central
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner for Aidan O'Brien with Ryan Moore; exceptional record on similar going (5W from 5 comparable runs), three-year-old who has won at the trip on good ground — the booking of Moore and the dominant form profile make this one of the most compelling entries.|
runners_data.comment: Confirmed the improvement shown as a two-year-old by winning a Listed sprint at Naas last time out, and still progressing with a top course jockey aboard; the step back to five furlongs from stall 24 on 127 lb may test, as connections likely prefer six.

races.paceDynamic: Big Mojo is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with Tom Marquand in the saddle, will set out to dictate from stall to line over this straight five furlongs on Good to Firm ground — a surface that rewards horses who can sustain their early pace rather than those who need cut. However, the field is saturated with natural prominent types: Night Raider, American Affair, Cover Up, Overpass, Mission Central, and Asfoora all want to race in the first two or three, meaning Big Mojo will not dictate in isolation and the early tempo will be genuinely strong. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, and of the redistributed horses Rosy Affair, Rayevka, Jakajaro, and Shagraan are most likely to secure a forward berth, while others such as Frost At Dawn, First Instinct, Getreadytorumble, and Aspect Island will be shuffled back against their natural inclination. A strong, honest gallop on quick ground over five furlongs at Ascot historically suits horses racing in midfield to hold-up positions who can pick up the pieces from a fast pace — horses with a high cruising speed and a clean late kick will be at a premium here.

watchPoints.text: With 26 runners and a field saturated by prominent types, watch for a chaotic early stages where horses like Jakajaro, Shagraan and Rosy Affair, all natural front-runners redistributed by the map, battle for positions they cannot all hold — those forced widest or furthest back against their style are at serious risk of never getting into the race.

Mission Central's record on similar going (5 wins from 5 comparable runs) under Ryan Moore for O'Brien makes him an obvious market mover — if he gets a clean trip from whatever draw he receives, his form entitles him to dominate, and a poor draw in a straight-five 26-runner field could be the difference between winning and defeat.

Big Mojo sets the pace but his last four runs show a declining trajectory (7th, 10th, 1st, 5th) and his win came at 6f — Tom Marquand must judge the tempo carefully or risk burning him out before the final furlong on quick going.

races.name: St James's Palace Stakes (Group 1) (Colts)

runners_data.name: Bow Echo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with four wins from four all on Good ground; Billy Loughnane can dictate terms as sole leader, 45 days off is not a concern given the unbeaten record and peak fitness implied by his OR of 126; the key question is whether his lead will be fast enough to test rivals or slow enough to invite a sprint finish he may not win.
runners_data.comment: Four wins on the spin culminate in a dominant 3-length 2000 Guineas success, where Bow Echo travelled supremely and quickened clear — a performance that marks him as the one to beat here, with proven course-and-distance form and 45 days to recover in good order.

runners_data.name: Gstaad
runners_data.note: A natural prominent type; Ryan Moore will aim to lock in the prime position immediately behind Bow Echo, and his seven-from-eight record on similar going is the standout statistical case in the race; the defeat on Firm ground is noted but Good to Firm suits based on his overall profile.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up in the Irish 2,000 Guineas last time, quickening smartly to win by three lengths and advertise top-class mile form; proven on today's going and distance, with a top course jockey aboard from stall 1, though reversing Newmarket form remains the chief task.

runners_data.name: Lord Britain
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner, but with four confirmed prominent types ahead of him in the pecking order, he is mapped to midfield as a consequence of this race shape — he is almost certain to race further back than ideal; OR of 88 is a significant class gap and his sim-going record of 0 wins from 2 placings on similar ground does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Lord Britain won a handicap at Kempton last time on the all-weather, but is yet to prove effectiveness on turf and looks out of depth here; the first-time headgear may help, but this trip and surface combination remains unproven and our figures rank him last of six.

runners_data.name: Power Blue
runners_data.note: A true prominent type by running style, but with a congested position battle developing he is redistributed to midfield on the map — he will likely race wider or deeper than his preferred spot; four from eight on similar going is solid but his recent form string (31-274) shows a slide and OR of 109 puts him well below the principals.
runners_data.comment: Power Blue showed Group 1 credentials when fourth in the Irish 2,000 Guineas last time but faces a re-opposing rival it couldn't beat there, and ranked fifth of six on our figures, a repeat performance looks unlikely to be enough here.

runners_data.name: Puerto Rico
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner and prominent type who has been mapped to midfield because the position is oversubscribed; Soumillon will face a difficult decision whether to fight for position or settle, and his wins came on Heavy ground at the Curragh which makes the step to Good to Firm a genuine query despite his Group 1 class.
runners_data.comment: Puerto Rico brings a fine recent profile with two G1 victories to its name and an upward curve through the backend of last season, and a closing fourth in the Poule d'Essai at Longchamp on its return suggests the spark remains — the key question is whether it can reproduce that form on quicker ground today.

runners_data.name: Talk Of New York
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner, but shown in midfield because the race shape cannot accommodate all prominent types at the front; William Buick is the jockey most likely to manufacture a clean prominent position regardless, and his three wins from four with two on Good ground make him a strong tactical candidate; the headgear flag warrants monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in its last four starts, including a scintillating 5½-length Listed victory at Sandown last time out, mark Talk Of New York as a serious threat; a trainer in form and a step up to today's mile suiting ideally, though first-time headgear adds a small unknown at this higher level.

races.paceDynamic: Bow Echo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with five prominent-style rivals all likely jostling for position behind him, he will set a genuine but uncontested lead — Billy Loughnane can dictate tempo on his own terms, which historically at Ascot over a mile on Good to Firm translates to a controlled early gallop that quickens markedly from the two-furlong pole. The five remaining runners — Gstaad, Puerto Rico, Talk Of New York, Power Blue, and Lord Britain — are all naturally prominent types, meaning the race shape will compress into a tight, tactical band directly behind the leader rather than spreading across the track, with significant barging and position-fighting through the downhill bend. This creates a race where the winner is most likely to come from the group that can settle just off the leader in the first two slots behind Bow Echo and then produce a clean, unimpeded turn of foot into the straight — a premium on tactical sharpness and the ability to switch off early before quickening late. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure their natural positions; Bow Echo is certain to lead, while Gstaad (Ryan Moore, Ballydoyle) and Talk Of New York (William Buick, Appleby) have the jockey craft and profile to most likely lock in the next positions, leaving Puerto Rico, Power Blue, and Lord Britain to race wider or deeper than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bow Echo Controls, Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If Bow Echo dictates a moderate early pace unchallenged and has enough left to kick off the home turn
scenarios.body: Bow Echo's unbeaten record over this course configuration and his four wins all on Good ground give him the platform to convert a lone leader's advantage into a wire-to-wire result; his OR of 126 and consistent TS profile mean rivals forcing a messy tactical race behind him only aid his cause

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Cover Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the race becomes a true test of finishing speed from the two-furlong pole
scenarios.body: Gstaad's seven runs on similar going with three wins and strong placed record mark him as the most reliable closer from just off the pace in a truly-run mile; Talk Of New York's two wins from three starts on Good ground and Buick's track craft give him the profile to produce a clean sprint finish from second or third

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Cavalry Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack refuses to settle behind Bow Echo and a fierce pace develops from the outset
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end gallop stretches the field and turns this into a stamina and class test, favouring horses who have shown the ability to race with cover and finish strong rather than those who burn petrol fighting for position; Puerto Rico's winning profile on Heavy and the step back to Good-to-Firm is a query, but his Group 1 form stands up

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent log-jam creates interference through the turn and the principals are checked or squeezed
scenarios.body: Lord Britain is the biggest beneficiary of a messy race where superior horses lose momentum; Talk Of New York's headgear flag and Power Blue's recent drop in form are concerns, but chaos neutralises class and gives lower-OR runners a route through

watchPoints.text: Bow Echo is entirely alone on the front end — if Billy Loughnane sets a falsely slow pace, the compressed prominent group behind will explode into a sprint at the two-furlong pole and he may be swamped.

The five prominent-style runners behind Bow Echo will create significant position-fighting through the downhill bend at Ascot — watch for Talk Of New York and Puerto Rico in particular being squeezed or forced wide, potentially costing them the race.
Puerto Rico's form on Good to Firm is thin (1 win from 6 similar-going runs) compared to his Heavy-ground wins at the Curragh — Soumillon may find him underperforming on this faster surface.

Lord Britain's OR of 88 represents a 38-pound gap to Bow Echo at the top of the weights — unless this race descends into complete chaos, the form book strongly suggests he is outclassed at Group 1 level.

Ryan Moore on Gstaad is the most important jockey move to track from the stalls — if Moore slots in directly behind Bow Echo within the first two furlongs, Gstaad's strong similar-going profile makes him the most positionally advantaged horse in the race.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who gets an uncontested lead here, which is a significant tactical advantage; won over 15f on similar going and is dropping back from 16f+ recent runs, but 2m4f is a stretch — his lead will be comfortable but the question is whether his stamina sees him home in a 20-runner field
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but shaped with plenty of promise before flopping over a sharp trip last time; back up in distance today suits ideally, acts on this going, and first-time headgear could sharpen focus — though the trainer's current form gives pause.

runners_data.name: Bunting
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up stayer returning from 248 days off for Willie Mullins with a claiming rider, but has solid form at 20f on Good and has run well fresh before; the long absence is the key concern but Mullins has form waking horses up first time out
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last four starts and found little when comfortably held last time, Bunting's best form has come over staying trips on the Flat, though it looks stable second string here and inconsistency over hurdles remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Barnso
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-riding type whose recent form shows consistent placed efforts at 14-18f; as a 3-year-old stepping up sharply to 2m4f, the trip looks a stretch and the 248 days off adds further risk
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts with a string of fourths before a below-par latest effort, Barnso is winless in its last five but the step up to 14f-plus looks key — stamina questions loom on reappearance after 248 days off, however.

runners_data.name: Reaching High
runners_data.note: Prominent-rider trained by Mullins, returning from 364 days absent having shown his best form at around 2m on Good ground; Ryan Moore takes the ride which is a significant upgrade, and his win over 14f at The Curragh gives hope, but this trip and the absence combine as concerns
runners_data.comment: Unlucky not to have won this 12 months ago when never getting a clear run and eased down beaten four lengths off the same mark, Reaching High lines up off an unchanged rating with course form and a top jockey aboard — the layoff is the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Lavender Hill Mob
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up stayer who won over 21f on Soft and has form over 16f on Good; the step up to 2m4f on faster ground suits the profile but he can be inconsistent — cheekpieces worn here
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and below par in recent outings, Lavender Hill Mob faces a stiff mark at 94, though the first-time visor and effectiveness across any going are mild positives worth monitoring after a 60-day break.

runners_data.name: Mordor
runners_data.note: Prominent-riding type in excellent form having won last time at 14f on Heavy for Gordon Elliott; has strong Good-ground form and placed effort at 24f suggests the trip is not a problem — a compelling profile if he can get his position in this congested field
runners_data.comment: Scored off a 7lb lower mark three starts back but was outstayed stepped up in trip last time; drops a significant 30lb here on a sound surface that suits, and proven course-and-distance form gives it every chance despite the inconsistent recent profile.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner who has placed at 14-20f on Good and Heathpark; consistent placed record for Joseph O'Brien but without a win on Good ground so far at this level — Colin Keane takes the ride
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when a close fourth at Chester last time off a 1lb lower mark, and this unexposed stayer's fine recent profile — including a runner-up effort — plus a significant jockey booking make her a leading danger, though she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Comfort Zone
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-riding type but carries headgear (blinkers) and has a recent pulled-up run that is a serious concern; the form book shows inconsistency and that run flags a fitness or soundness question
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and pulled up at Cork latest when the ground proved too testing, Comfort Zone is only 1lb higher than when placing in this race last year, giving it a clear angle — though below-par form this term is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Siempre Arturo
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer whose best form is at 12f on Tapeta and Standard; this step up to 2m4f on Good turf looks a considerable stamina ask — form over the trip and on this surface is unproven
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces and a 38-day break since a run that needed, Siempre Arturo has the versatility across trips and surfaces to be competitive, but patchy recent form and the step up in trip still required leave this one looking a place player at best.

runners_data.name: Defiantly
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse running in blinkers for Joseph O'Brien; best form at 12-14f and on Soft ground, so the 2m4f trip and Good to Firm going both look against him despite James Doyle taking the ride
runners_data.comment: Blinkers go on for the first time and there's a distance uptick that could suit this lightly-raced stayer, but inconsistent recent form and a lowly ranking on our figures make it hard to fancy with confidence.
